newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla changing juices after outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla changing juices after outbreak.

text.p: Odwalla Inc chief executive officer Stephen Williamson said Monday the company is reformulating some products to eliminate apple juice, which has been implicated in an bacterial poisoning outbreak.
"We are in the process of reformulating a number of drinks which we will soon put back on the shelf," Williamson told reporters by telephone at a news conference.

He said the company had no plans to reintroduce any products containing carrot juice until the company "can unravel the mystery" of how its products came to be tainted with a potentially lethal strain of E. coli bacteria.

An Odwalla spokeswoman said the fruit juice producer was reformulating 12 juice-based drinks that were recalled last week, but she could not say when they would be reintroduced to the market or whether the reformulations would be permanent.

The company last week voluntarily recalled apple juice and 12 beverages containing apple juice after epidemiologists in Washington state established a link between Odwalla juice and the outbreak that has sickened at least 39.
Later the company recalled carrot juice and a vegetable cocktail that are made on the same line as the apple drinks.
The potentially lethal E. coli O157:H7 bacteria can get into the food chain through contact with cattle, goat or deer faeces.

U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) director David Kessler said it was too early to say whether the agency would seek to require all apple juice to be pasteurised or would order new labeling for fresh juice.
"We are still in the process of determining what caused this outbreak," he said by telephone. "I think the public has to know that there certainly is some risk in drinking unpasteurised apple juice."
While Williamson said the outbreak posed questions for the "fresh juice and fresh food industries", Kessler limited his cautionary comments to unpasteurised apple juice.

He noted that so far outbreaks of E. coli O157:H7 have been traced conclusively only to ground beef, lettuce and fresh apple juice. Earlier federal officials said they had found E. coli O157:H7 in an Odwalla apple juice sample, and they were confident further testing would establish a conclusive link to victims of the outbreak.
"We think that the microbiological confirmation is helpful," Williamson said. "It's another piece of evidence that can help us all unravel this mystery." -- Martin Wolk 206-386-4848
